study type: secondary analysis of a national, prospective cohort study
cohort: 4436 pregnant women admitted to hospital in the UK with symptomatic SARS-CoV-2 from March 1, 2020 to October 31, 2021
finding: Pregnant women with severe COVID-19 were more likely to be older, overweight or obese, of mixed ethnicity, have gestational diabetes, and experience adverse outcomes including pre-labor cesarean birth, preterm birth, stillbirth, and neonatal unit admission.
mod_finding: Women with severe infection were more likely to have a pre-labor cesarean birth compared to those with mild or moderate infection (aOR 8.84, 95% CI 6.61-11.83).
